description: Sequencer built from up to seven typed rules of scale-degree and duration pairs, where the last degree of a rule picks the rule that follows it, with every degree quantised to a scale set on the menu

params.text: Starts and stops the sequence, and the lamp in it is lit while the sequence runs
Restarts the sequence of every channel at the first rule

inputs.text: One pulse per beat drives everything; every duration written in a rule is counted in these pulses, and with nothing patched here the sequence never advances
A trigger restarts every channel at the first rule; with a cable in EVAL in Rule select mode it jumps straight to the first step of the rule that voltage picks
A trigger flips the sequence between running and stopped, exactly as the RUN button does
Steers which rule plays next, in whichever way the Eval input mode menu item is set to: a 0 to 10V rule number, a gate above 2V holding the current rule, or a trigger releasing the next transition

outputs.text: The pitch of the step playing on that channel, one volt per octave, quantised to the scale and root note set on the menu
10V while the step playing on that channel sounds, dropping briefly at each new step so that envelopes retrigger, and staying at 0V through a silence step
A 10V trigger when the rule playing on that channel finishes, with all of that rule's repetitions counting as one block
0V to 10V saying which rule that channel is playing, in steps of ten sixths of a volt, with 0V for the first rule and 10V for the seventh

notes: The module does nothing until a rule is typed into one of the seven text fields and a clock is patched.
A rule is written as an initiator degree and duration, then an arrow, then the steps of the sequence, each a degree and a duration separated by a comma.
The seven rule fields and the two random-pool fields below them are typed into directly, and confirmed with Enter or by clicking away.
A rule field's bar is yellow while it has focus, red when what is typed will not parse, and green while the first channel plays that rule.
Two clock pulses are needed before sub-beat timing is available; until then only the first step of each beat fires.
If the clock stops or a pulse arrives late, the pitch and gate hold where they are rather than running on.
Editing a rule that is currently playing takes effect only once that rule and all its repetitions have finished, so rules can be rewritten without stopping playback.
menu: Polyphony channels — sets how many independent voices run, from one to six; all four outputs carry that many channels, and each voice makes its own random choices
Reset when starting playback — restarts the sequence every time playback is started from the RUN button or the run input
If a note has no rule...: Loop back to first rule, Jump to a random rule — sets what happens when the last degree of a rule matches no other rule's initiator
Eval input mode: Rule select (0-10V CV), Loop / Hold rule (Gate), Advance on trigger (Trigger) — sets how the EVAL jack steers the sequence
Autoreset after steps (each step = 1 beat): Off, 8 beats, 16 beats, 32 beats, 64 beats — restarts the sequence automatically after that many clock pulses
Scale — sets the scale the rule degrees are quantised to, natural major by default
Root note — sets the tonic of that scale, C by default
Random degree range (r) — sets the limits the random character picks between when the degree pool is empty, and the limits the plus and minus operators wrap at
Randomize rules style: Melodic, Acid / Techno, Ambient / Evolving, Complex L-System — sets the profile used when Randomize Rules writes the rules
Randomize Rules — writes a fresh set of rules and both random pools in the chosen style; leave the seed field above it empty for a random seed, or type one in to repeat a particular result
